title: Post-upgrade secret mismatch causing operator reconciliation failures in on-prem clusters
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Summary: Several on-prem customers reported operator reconciliation loops and failing post-upgrade hooks after we rolled operator v2.6.2 -> v2.6.3 via Helm. Symptoms included 'Secret not owned by controller' errors, repeated restart of operator pods, and downstream component restarts (ingress-controller, sidecar proxies). Impact: customer production inference capacity degraded or briefly unavailable on Dedicated/Private clusters during and after upgrade.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - initial report from support: Customer ACME reported operator crashlooping after automated upgrade (region: eu-west-1-onprem). Escalated to infra oncall.

2026-03-10 10:05 - oncall (Liam) reproduced in lab cluster using the customer's helm values. Observed operator logs: 'failed to adopt secret: owner reference mismatch' followed by k8s events showing controller ref update attempts.
2026-03-10 13:30 - triage call with PM (Sofia Martinez), Support (Maya Li), and Engineering. Agreed this blocks further automatic upgrades until a hotfix is deployed and validated. P0 decision made.

2026-03-11 08:15 - root cause hypothesis: operator v2.6.3 introduces namespaced secret format change to support KMS key metadata. Helm upgrade preserved legacy secrets with different annotation/key layout; operator's new adoption logic rejected secrets owned previously by 'operator-controller' because the UID check failed when HK values were rewritten by helm hooks.
attachments: Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/482 - add backwards-compatible secret adoption and post-upgrade migration hook
Helm chart change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/commit/7d4b2f2 - add post-upgrade job 'migrate-operator-secrets'
resolution_summary: Root cause: a non-backwards-compatible secret owner/annotation shape change introduced in operator v2.6.3 resulted in the controller refusing to adopt existing secrets. Fix implemented in operator v2.6.3-hotfix: (1) controller accepts both legacy and new secret schemas during a 30-day compatibility window, (2) a Helm post-upgrade Job that atomically migrates legacy secrets to the new format and updates ownerReferences safely, and (3) additional validation to avoid double-adoption. Timeline: hotfix branch cut 2026-03-11, PR #482 opened 2026-03-12, hotfix image built and smoke-tested in staging 2026-03-13, canary pushed to three low-risk customer clusters 2026-03-14, monitoring shows no regression and reconciliation stabilized. A full rollout is scheduled after final sign-off on 2026-03-16.
next_steps: Complete canary rollout (target 10% of on-prem fleet) and monitor 72h metrics: reconciliation errors, operator pod restarts, inference latency SLOs
Backport hotfix to operator-2.5.x LTS branch for customers pinned to older minor releases
Add automated helm upgrade gate in our deployment pipeline to run migration job in dry-run mode before applying changes
Create an e2e test that covers secret schema migration and ownerReference preservation in the upgrade matrix (helm versions, k8s versions)
Post-mortem write-up and customer-facing RCA draft for Support to share with affected customers
